API reference

Scraper

Scrape publicly available GradCafe admissions results.

scrape.build_survey_url(cursor: str | None = None) → str

Construct a GradCafe survey URL with an optional pagination cursor.

scrape.capture_current_page(page_number: int) → Path

Capture and save the currently displayed public GradCafe survey page.

scrape.parse_captured_page(input_file: Path) → tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], str | None]

Parse applicant records and the next cursor URL from captured HTML.

scrape.save_data(records: list[dict[str, Any]], output_file: Path = PosixPath('/Users/karimzaky/Documents/jhu_software_concepts/module_4/applicant_data.json')) → None

Save records atomically so an interruption does not corrupt the JSON.

scrape.load_data(input_file: Path = PosixPath('/Users/karimzaky/Documents/jhu_software_concepts/module_4/applicant_data.json')) → list[dict[str, Any]]

Load previously saved records so scraping can resume.

scrape.scrape_data(target_records: int = 30000, max_pages: int | None = None) → list[dict[str, Any]]

Capture, parse, deduplicate, and checkpoint GradCafe records.

Cleaner

Clean and validate structured GradCafe applicant data.

clean.clean_data(records: list[dict[str, Any]]) → list[dict[str, Any]]

Clean records and remove duplicate applicant URLs.

clean.main() → None

Load, clean, validate, and save applicant records.

Data loader

Load the cleaned GradCafe applicant data into PostgreSQL.

load_data.get_connection()

Create a PostgreSQL connection using environment variables.

load_data.clean_text(value)

Convert blank text values to None for SQL NULL storage.

load_data.parse_number(value)

Extract a floating-point number from a labeled score string.

load_data.parse_bounded_number(value, minimum, maximum)

Extract a number and return it only when it falls within an accepted range.

Values outside the range are treated as missing because they cannot reliably represent the metric assigned to the column.

load_data.parse_date(value)

Convert a GradCafe date string into a Python date.

load_data.prepare_record(record)

Convert one JSON record into the database column format.

load_data.load_records(records=None)

Insert supplied records, or read records from the local JSON file.

Return the number of newly inserted rows. Database errors propagate to the caller, and the connection context rolls back failed inserts.

Raw SQL queries

Run the required GradCafe analyses using raw SQL.

query_data.run_raw_sql_queries()

Execute the raw SQL queries and print their formatted results.

ORM queries

Repeat selected Module 3 analyses using SQLAlchemy ORM.

orm_queries.get_question_1(session)

Return the number of Fall 2026 entries.

SQLAlchemy builds the SQL statement from the Applicant model.

orm_queries.get_question_2(session)

Return the percentage of usable nationality classifications that are International.

orm_queries.get_question_3(session)

Return the average GPA and three GRE metrics.

SQL AVG ignores NULL values independently for every column.

orm_queries.get_question_4(session)

Return the average GPA of American Fall 2026 applicants.

SQL AVG automatically ignores NULL GPA values.

orm_queries.get_question_5(session)

Return the percentage of Fall 2025 entries that are acceptances.

The main WHERE condition defines the denominator as all Fall 2025 entries. The filtered count defines the acceptance numerator.

orm_queries.get_question_6(session)

Return the average GPA of accepted Fall 2026 applicants.

orm_queries.get_question_7(session)

Return the Johns Hopkins Computer Science master’s count using the original program and degree fields.

orm_queries.original_university_conditions()

Return the university conditions used with the original program field.

The regular-expression operator recognizes MIT as a standalone abbreviation. This remains an SQLAlchemy expression and does not use handwritten SQL through text().

orm_queries.llm_university_conditions()

Return university conditions for the LLM-generated university field.

Both Georgetown and the observed George Town variation are included.

orm_queries.get_question_8(session)

Return the Question 8 count using the original program field.

Every expression passed to where() must be true for a record to contribute to the count.

orm_queries.get_question_9(session)

Return the Question 9 count using the LLM-generated fields.

Term, status, and degree remain based on the original downloaded fields, as required by the assignment.

orm_queries.get_original_question(session)

Compare Fall 2026 acceptance percentages for American and international applicants.

GROUP BY returns one result row for each nationality group.

orm_queries.get_question_11(session)

Return the five universities with the most reported Fall 2026 acceptances.

orm_queries.collect_all_analysis_results()

Collect every analysis required by the Flask webpage.

All database reads use SQLAlchemy ORM expressions and the Applicant model.

orm_queries.collect_orm_results()

Execute all required ORM analyses and return their results.

Keeping the query logic in reusable functions allows the Flask application to import these functions later.

orm_queries.print_orm_results(results)

Print the ORM results using the assignment’s required formats.

orm_queries.main()

Collect and display the required SQLAlchemy ORM analyses.

Flask application and routes

Run the dynamic Flask analysis webpage for Module 3.

app.format_metric(value, suffix='')

Format available numbers to two decimals; show N/A when missing.

app.build_view_model(raw_results)

Convert raw SQLAlchemy values into display-ready strings.

Formatting values here keeps presentation formatting out of the database queries and makes the HTML template easier to read.

app.analysis()

Query PostgreSQL through SQLAlchemy and display the analysis page.

Every page request retrieves the current database results rather than displaying hard-coded values.

app.pull_data()

Start a pull when idle and report its status as JSON.

app.update_analysis()

Refresh analysis only when no data pull is running.

app.create_app(test_config=None)

Create a configurable Flask application.

app.main()

Start the local Flask development server.

Background pull manager

Manage background scraping for the Module 3 Flask application.

scrape_manager.get_scrape_status()

Return a safe copy of the current scraping status.

scrape_manager.start_data_pull()

Start one background data pull.

Return False when another scrape already owns the lock, preventing simultaneous Chrome navigation and duplicate scraping processes.
